question.text: Under Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013, the Registrar of Companies (ROC) has the power to:

answer.text: Strike a defunct company off the register after prescribed formalities
Issue securities on behalf of the company

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013 gives the Registrar of Companies the power to strike a defunct company off the register after completing the prescribed formalities. The Trap: Appointing directors, approving M&A and issuing securities are functions of the company / its shareholders / NCLT / SEBI respectively - not ROC powers under Section 248. The strike-off power is specifically a Registrar function. Note: Page 36 of the workbook supports the Section 248 strike-off power vested in the Registrar.
